chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fazalah, from Aban, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked, 'A man prays while he is seated, and recites the Chapter. When he intends to conclude it, he stands and performs Ruku' at the end of it.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'His prayer is the prayer of the standing one.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a person's prayer if they stand up while seated to finish reciting the Quran?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), this hadith clarifies that a seated worshipper who stands to complete their recitation retains the full reward and validity of a standing prayer, highlighting the Shia juristic principle of accommodating physical ease without compromising ritual integrity. This ruling is frequently cited in discussions on the 'Salat al-Mufaddal' and the flexibility of postures for the elderly or sick, ensuring that the act of standing for recitation does not invalidate the prayer if the individual is unable to maintain it throughout. It underscores the Shia emphasis on the continuity of the prayer's spiritual state over rigid adherence to a single posture when necessity dictates.
